problem.para: With the current specification, it is not possible to write a single SQL-invoked routine whose input is a generic MD-array type with an unspecified (or maximum) dimension and use that routine to operate on any MD-array with a concrete (or lower than maximum) dimension and have logic within the routine to distinguish the different dimensions. Instead what needs to be done is to write n routines (where n is the number of different dimensions that need to be dealt with) and duplicate the programming logic (and maintenance effort) n times. For n > 2, this may become a usability issue.
It should be easily possible to cast a 1-dimensional MD-array to a regular array and vice versa.

Currently the lower and upper limits for an MD-axis are restricted to be literals. It could be beneficial to make them more dynamic to allow the limits of one MD-array type to be based on the limits of another existing MD-array (value).
Similar considerations apply for the names of the MD-axes and the whole MD-extent.

With the current specification, it is not possible to write a single SQL-invoked routine whose input is a generic MD-array type with an unspecified (or maximum) dimension and use that routine to operate on any MD-array with a concrete (or lower than maximum) dimension and have logic within the routine to distinguish the different dimensions. Instead what needs to be done is to write n routines (where n is the number of different dimensions that need to be dealt with) and duplicate the programming logic (and maintenance effort) n times. For n > 2, this may become a usability issue.

Given an n-dimensional MD-array X, it may be beneficial to define an alias Y for it that has less dimensions ( Y[i] = X[i, i], or Y[x, y] = X[f(x), g(y), h(x, y), ) and then use that alias in a query (declared in the WITH clause) or in a PSM block (declared in the DECLARE section). The alias would not be a new value but just a pointer into the existing MD-array.
Ada provides the method of aggregate notation, both positional and named, to initialize a multidimensional array. Similar functionality would be beneficial for MD-arrays as well.
